rows.04:6964:
"Don't give me that!
You beat him to a pulp too, didn't you?"
They all started pinning the blame on each other.
But that wasn't going to get them anywhere.
So in the end, they all agreed to cover the whole thing up.
How, you ask?
They pretended to be victims too.
Faked it, basically.{p}
rows.04:6a9c:
Just like the seniors, they made it look like somebody had drugged them and beaten them black and blue.
They all punched each other, lay down in the same place as the seniors, and waited for somebody to find them.{p}
rows.04:6b64:
That 'somebody' didn't show up until the next morning.
An alumnus who'd come to put his beloved juniors through the wringer found them all lying in the dining hall.
"What the hell happened here★"
Can't blame the guy for being shocked.
The toughest fighters of a boxing club ranked among the best in the country were sprawled on the floor in a pitiful state.
"Call the police!"
"No, an ambulance!"
I hear it was total chaos.
In the end, a paralyzing drug was found on the dishes left at the scene, and it was ruled the work of someone with a grudge against the boxing club.{p}
rows.04:6d50:
A club member who couldn't take the seniors' hazing and ran away...
A rival school's boxing club that always lost to them in matches...
Back then, there were mountains of people with a grudge against the boxing club.
It all went exactly the way Akasaka had scripted it.{p}
rows.04:6e38:
What's wrong, {a}?
Why the scary face...
Does it bug you that much that Akasaka and the others got away with their cover-up?
You think they should've been punished, right?
Man, you're an impatient one.
Well, just hear my story out to the end.{p}
rows.04:6f1c:
Their injuries were pretty light compared to the other seniors'.
It was all faked, after all.
On top of that, the second- and third-years who were the club's core were too hurt to move, right?
So ironically, it fell to Akasaka and the other first-years to carry the boxing club.{p}
rows.04:7004:
And get this: Akasaka, of all people, was racking up some pretty impressive results.
Maybe something changed inside him after that incident, huh?
Like he'd found out how good it felt to hit people... you know.
He'd always had guts, so I think he had the talent for it.{p}
rows.04:70fc:
...And then a year went by.
They were second-years now.
This time it was their turn to put the first-years through hell.
The first-years that year had real rotten luck.{p}
rows.04:7260:
Nobody said it out loud, but everyone involved in the incident a year earlier couldn't hide how uneasy they were.
Akasaka was no different.
If he'd had his way, maybe he wouldn't have gone to the summer camp at all.
But that wasn't an option, right?
If one of them said he wasn't going, you know the rest would all say they were skipping it too.
After all, they were accomplices.{p}
rows.04:73b4:
Akasaka and the others hazed and hazed them without letup.
Even when somebody collapsed, they never cut them any slack.
And one after another, more of them ran away.
For those guys, maybe hazing the first-years was the only way to take their minds off their fear, you know?
Then one day...{p}
rows.04:74a4:
It was right at dinnertime.
The first-year on meal duty mumbled something under their breath.{p}
rows.04:74f4:
"There's no sleeping drug or paralyzing drug in this miso soup..."
With that, the kid held out a bowl of miso soup to Akasaka.
"..........★"
They say that as Akasaka and the other second-years stared at the kid in shock, their faces went pale and twisted with terror right before everyone's eyes.
From that day on, the second-years stopped eating altogether.{p}
rows.04:760c:
They figured this time it was their turn to get payback from the first-years.
Had somebody figured out the truth about what happened a year ago★
But who...?
This one...★
...This one was laughing at me just now.
Or was it that one?
No, that one's eyes look shifty too...
Agh, I don't know...
Once those second-years started thinking like that, they couldn't stop.
They say just having anyone besides themselves come near scared them out of their wits.{p}
rows.04:7798:
Barely eating anything in the heat of high summer, they all wasted away fast.
Against their dark, sunburned skin, only their eyes glittered with a weird, feverish light.
Ever seen a boxer cutting weight?
The kind who has to go without not just food but even water.
They looked just like that.
You think a body can hold up doing that while it's still growing?
They say by the time the camp ended, they were in pretty bad shape.{p}
rows.04:7904:
They made it down the mountain on their own, but went straight into the hospital.
See?
They got punished after all, didn't they?
And that's not all, either.{p}
rows.04:79a0:
That day, when Akasaka and the others stopped eating...
They say there wasn't a single first-year left at the camp.
There weren't many to begin with, and then they dropped out one after another.
Less than a week into the camp, every last first-year was gone.
So who made dinner that day, I wonder?{p}
rows.04:7b90:
Maybe it was despair over that, but every one of them vanished from their hospital rooms before they were even discharged.
All the first-years had dropped out, and most of the third-years were still in rehab, right?
With every second-year gone missing on top of that, there was no way the club could keep going.
That's why the boxing club went downhill.{p}
rows.04:7c98:
Oh yeah, a rumor got around that the ghosts of boxers worn down to skin and bones haunt that training camp lodge.
I think it started right around when Akasaka and the others disappeared.{p}
rows.04:7d30:
They say those ghosts keep on sparring in a ring that's like a red-hot iron plate, letting out groans of agony.
Limp, their upper bodies slumped forward like this, almost like they're bowing in apology, they just keep slugging each other.
Somebody said it looked like a dance.
Others said they heard the sound of someone pounding a punching bag...
Lots of people love going to places like that, right?
So there's no shortage of info.
If you're curious, go check it out sometime.
That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.04:7f14:
Yeah, believe it or not, Akasaka said that if they talked like that, he'd tell on them to the seniors.
Akasaka had no intention of running away at all.
But if the other first-years ran off, he'd be the only one left to take all the hazing, right?
He was trying to stop that from happening.
Here's what Akasaka said:
"We've held out this long.
Let's make it through to the end.
If you're really planning to run, I'll stop you, even if I have to tell the seniors.
But don't worry.
If you give up on running, I swear I won't tell..."
But hey, hear something like that, and the guys who'd suggested running would start getting nervous, right?
"Okay.
We won't run."
That's what they told him, but at the same time, they were all thinking:
Even if we really do give up on running...{p}
rows.04:81ac:
"W-We'd better go get the seniors, anyway."
When one of them blurted that out in a panic, Hatanaka cut in.
"Hold on, how're we gonna explain this?
You gonna report that we lynched him to keep him quiet about the escape?"
He had a point.
Everyone went silent.
Then Hatanaka, checking that no seniors were around, came out with this.{p}
rows.04:82dc:
"Listen up, I've got a good idea.
First, we carry Akasaka's body to his futon and lay him down.
Then you go report to the seniors.
We make it look like Akasaka died from the seniors' hazing..."
Nobody objected to the plan.
The only reason the first-years had lynched Akasaka in the first place was that they were scared of the seniors' hazing.
If it weren't for the seniors' hazing, none of this would have happened.
Telling each other that, they set out to pin the crime on the seniors.{p}
rows.04:8478:
"Senpai!
Akasaka... Akasaka is dead☆"
When Hatanaka said that, pretending to go pale, the seniors fell for it, hook, line and sinker.
They started talking over how to hide Akasaka's body.
"How about we bury him?"
"No, they'd find him the second a search started."
"Then what do we do?"
"First we burn him.
We'll reduce him to bones so he's easier to hide."
The seniors were totally convinced it was their own fault.
"Once he's bones, where do we hide him?"
"Let's see, the best hiding place would be... that, wouldn't it?"{p}
rows.04:870c:
And then they each took a turn training on that punching bag.
All of them drove their fists into it, over and over and over.
The seniors ordered them to.
They wanted to drill one idea into everyone: even if the seniors were the ones who'd killed Akasaka, all of them had hidden the body.
Collective responsibility, I guess?
Burning Akasaka's body took until the middle of the night, so by the time they finished training on the bone-filled bag, it was dawn of the next day.
Hell of a story, huh?{p}
rows.04:8898:
From the next day on, the camp's usual hazing got toned down.
The seniors were jumpy as hell by then.
On the last day of camp, they even went so far as to suggest just having some normal practice matches.
"That sounds great."
Somebody answered under their breath.
It sounded like Akasaka's voice.
But the seniors didn't bother checking who had answered, and had the first-years start setting up for the matches.
"All right, we're doing practice matches.
First up, Hatanaka, you."
Hatanaka stepped into the ring and looked at the senior who'd climbed in ahead of him. Or so he should have.{p}
rows.04:8a8c:
But the one in the ring with his fists up was...
"A-Akasaka..."
The senior was nowhere to be seen.
Standing there was Akasaka, wearing bright red gloves.
And what's more, a stench like rotting leather was drifting off Akasaka's gloves.{p}
rows.04:8b6c:
"Aaaaaaagh!"
Screaming, Hatanaka flew at him, swinging wildly.
But Akasaka came at him swinging just as wildly.
The guys watching around the ring were so overwhelmed by the bizarre sight that for a while they couldn't do a thing.
And then, the moment they'd both been beaten to shreds and were about to black out...
Hatanaka saw it.{p}
rows.04:8c98:
Saw Akasaka, standing in the ring, turn into the senior.
And he heard it, too.
Heard these words come out of the senior's mouth:
"Forgive me, Akasaka..."{p}
rows.04:8d38:
The two of them went down in the ring, unconscious and in critical condition.
Then the rest climbed into the ring one by one as if drawn there, trading punches and dropping.
Every one of them saw whoever they were fighting as Akasaka.
After that, they all lay collapsed in the ring for a long time.
They were found by a search party the school sent, and every one of them survived, but...{p}
rows.04:8e84:
After that, Akasaka came back to school too.
Akasaka, who should've been killed, burned down to bones and stuffed in a punching bag, came back a few days later.
And he kept on coming to school.
Akasaka was supposed to be dead.
And yet...
Nobody except the ones who'd gone to the camp thought anything of Akasaka being there.
But the boxing club guys who'd been at the camp all went white as a sheet.{p}
rows.04:8fcc:
Because they knew that the Akasaka who showed up to every practice wasn't really of this world.
And then, something happened again.
The ones who'd had a hand in Akasaka's murder started disappearing, one after another.
It's not that they killed themselves, or got murdered.
They all just went missing before anybody noticed.
And word is, every time that happened, the boxing club's punching bag got a little bigger.
Because of that, ugly rumors spread about the boxing club, and for a while it nearly went under.
Before every member was gone, the school figured something was off and had an exorcism done.
And they say Akasaka vanished for good.{p}
rows.04:92c0:
...{a}, go check out the boxing club sometime.
It's not much of a club these days.
But there's one thing about it that's really something.
I'll tell you what.{p}
rows.04:93cc:
That's right.
Here's what Hatanaka came out with.{p}
rows.04:9404:
I see.
So that's what you think.
Well, maybe it really would've been better if he hadn't gone.
But Hatanaka didn't do that.
He couldn't.
Think about it.
Hatanaka was the leader of the second-year group.
If he didn't go, the others wouldn't want to go either, and he'd lose his grip on them.
If the second-years all skipped it at once, people would be sure to start asking why.
And then there'd be no telling whether somebody might start talking.
Hatanaka had no choice.{p}
rows.04:97c8:
They weren't gloves.
Two bloody hands, torn off at the wrist, were gripping Hatanaka's fists...
What he'd thought were red gloves were severed hands, wet with red blood.
"Waaaaaaaagh☆"
Screaming, Hatanaka tried to shake off the bloody hands.
Then the hands let go of his... and slapped onto Hatanaka's face with a wet splat.
The guys who were there hurried to get help.
And when everyone came running, Hatanaka was saying this:
"It was my fault!
Akasaka... it was my fault..."{p}
rows.04:99ac:
And that's how the club members found out that Hatanaka and the others had killed Akasaka.
Hatanaka and the others were expelled and got the punishment they had coming, so I hear.
After that, there was no more hazing in the boxing club.
They didn't practice much anymore, and the club itself shrank a lot.
That's the kind of incident that made our boxing club go to seed.
Of course, officially, they keep quiet about there being a murder, or about Akasaka's hands turning up.{p}
rows.04:9b64:
Akasaka's body was given a proper burial.
But...
It seems his love for boxing still hasn't faded, even now.
I hear he sometimes shows up during the boxing club's matches.
Akasaka's ghost, I mean.
They say he watches the boxers in the match with envy...
That's the end of my story.
Now, let's hear the next one...{p}
rows.04:9c90:
Yeah, Hatanaka went to the place where they'd buried the body.
And what does he find but the outline of a person laid out on the dirt in white rope.
"No way...
Did somebody find Akasaka's body here...?"
Hatanaka touched the dirt there with trembling hands.
...There was no sign it had been dug up.
Then what was this rope...?
Behind Hatanaka, he heard something stir.
"Hatanaka.
That rope marks the spot for someone who's about to die.
And that someone is... you.
They're going to find you lying right here."
Akasaka was behind Hatanaka.
Akasaka's ghost was riding on Hatanaka's back, clinging to him like a kid getting a piggyback.
So even when Hatanaka turned around, he couldn't see Akasaka.
"Akasaka★
Where are you?
Where the hell are you★"
Hatanaka thrashed around blindly.
Spinning around, swinging his arms, kicking at the air...
But he couldn't see Akasaka anywhere, and only that voice kept ringing right in his ear.
And then...{p}
rows.04:9fc4:
Feeling Akasaka clinging to his back, Hatanaka drove his fists into his own body again and again.
Over and over.{p}
rows.04:a040:
The next day, Hatanaka was found dead inside the white rope outline.
They say the moment the first-year who found him laid eyes on it, the white rope vanished like smoke.
And they say a glove had been stuffed into dead Hatanaka's mouth.
A glove as red as blood.{p}
rows.04:a14c:
{a}.
That's the kind of incident that made the boxing club go to seed.
And as if following Hatanaka in death, the others in his year died one after another.
Apparently each of them tore up their own body with their own fists.
And after that, whenever there was hazing in the boxing club, whoever did the hazing would always end up in an accident later...{p}
rows.04:a2a0:
That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next person tell theirs...{p}
rows.04:a2e0:
Scared to find out?
I don't think you'd get cursed just from looking at Hatanaka's photo.
Well, if that's how you feel, I won't force you.
All right, let's hear the next story, then.
Who's gonna tell us the next one...?{p}
rows.04:a42c:
"{a}, don't you feel a chill?
If we stop now, something even more horrible is bound to happen.
I have that feeling."
That was what one of them said.{p}
rows.04:a4b8:
"Come on, we've come this far, so let's tell the stories to the end.
And then we'll see it through.
See how this gathering ends."
The other one pressed me hard.
...What's going on?
Why are these two saying things like this?
Just a little while ago, they'd looked so uneasy.
It was as if something had possessed them.
A tense air filled the club room.
In the hush, only my heartbeat echoed.
The two of them were silently waiting for my answer.
"I really think we should stop..."
I'm a coward.{p}
rows.04:a6a4:
I told the two of them we should stop, and without waiting for an answer, I tried to rush out of the club room.
And then...
"{a}, you're going to be cursed..."
A voice came from behind me.
Cursed?
Me...?
I didn't turn around, and left the club room.{p}
rows.04:a784:
Then I heard the two of them laughing in the club room.
Maybe they were laughing at me.{p}
rows.04:a888:
When I got to school the next day, Hino was lying dead on the teacher's platform in my classroom.
On Hino's cheek was a cut in the shape of the character for 'curse.'
Several streaks of blood had trickled down from the wound.
I had a bad feeling.
Should we have told the seven wonders' ghost stories to the very end?
And would tracking down whatever had been menacing us and fighting it have been the best way?
But there's no turning back time now.
Just then, I felt a sharp sting on my hand.
Wondering what it was, I looked down...{p}
rows.04:aa60:
On the back of my hand was a cut in the shape of the character for 'curse.'
Am I next...?
I lowered my eyes.
And I pictured myself surrendering to my fate.
That me was smeared bright red with blood.
Bright red, smeared bright red with blood...{p}
